title: Employee Tenure in Full Years
description:
Calculate how many **full years** each employee has worked at the company, based on their `hire_date` relative to a reference date of **2026-09-01**.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| hire_date | DATE |

Output columns: `name`, `hire_date`, `tenure_years`. Order by `tenure_years` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, hire_date DATE); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice',DATE '2020-01-15'),(2,'Bob',DATE '2022-06-01'),(3,'Carol',DATE '2015-11-20'),(4,'Dan',DATE '2024-03-10'),(5,'Eve',DATE '2026-09-01');
solution_sql: SELECT name, hire_date, DATE_DIFF('year', hire_date, DATE '2026-09-01') AS tenure_years FROM employees ORDER BY tenure_years DESC

test_cases.description: Carol has the longest tenure; Eve has 0 (same day)

hints: DATE_DIFF('year', start_date, end_date) computes the difference in full years in DuckDB.
Eve was hired exactly on the reference date, so her tenure is 0.
